title: fix(record): release cancelled, closed and crashed takes; stop encoding at stop; no orphan media
body:
Fixes seven findings from the audit of the recording hub, the recorder store, the engine and the disk writer. Each one is a real path that loses state, leaks a device, or leaves a take in an inconsistent place. The control bar's "Saving…" leftover and the countdown setting are **not** in this PR (they are handled separately).

What changes, in one line each:

- **Cancel while the take's file is being created** no longer starts the engine (the screen and mic stayed open for good).
- **Pause/resume** are ignored outside `recording` / `paused` (a pause during finalize moved the store out of `finalizing`).
- **Window closed during the countdown** releases the pending take (tray, Esc, shade).
- **Renderer crash during a countdown** reveals the app the countdown had hidden.
- **Dead renderer's takes** release their file handles; session ids are unique across renderer restarts.
- **Stop** stops encoding right away instead of after the 1 s poster-frame wait.
- **Metadata failure after the move** takes the media back to staging, so no orphan `.mp4` sits in the vault and the take stays salvageable.

## Update after the agent review (2026-10-27)

- `main` merged in (6dd5452d). #395 landed the same pause/resume guard; the only conflict was its comment. #395's per-take generation and aborted cursor-track ids sit next to this branch's unique session ids without overlap.
- **`releaseAll` is now wired** (1ace9f4f): the hub's `forceReset` calls it. Both the window's `closed` handler and `render-process-gone` go through `forceReset`. Before this, the "dead renderer's takes release their file handles" line above was not true: nothing called it.
- **A failed take-back offers no salvage** (a743ca0f): if the media cannot be moved back to staging, it stays in the vault (listed without a sidecar), and the original error is thrown instead of a `FinalizeMoveError` that pointed at a missing file.
- Checks at a743ca0f: `vitest run` (apps/kaipu-record) 286 files / 2650 tests passed; `check-types` 0; lint 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean; `check-workflows` 0; pre-push `verify-local` passed.

## How to reproduce

**Not reproduced in the app.** Every finding comes from reading the code. The tests below reproduce them: on `main`, the cases marked *red* fail, and they pass on this branch. Run them from `apps/kaipu-record`:

| Finding | Reproduce (test) | On `main` | Manual check in the app |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cancel during file creation starts the engine | `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.test.ts -t "before main confirms"` | red | Not practical: needs a slow disk. |
| Pause during finalize | `... recorder-store.test.ts -t "ignored while the take is finalizing"` | red | Not practical: needs a stop that takes time. |
| Dead renderer's sessions / id reuse | `npx vitest run src/main/recording/recording-writer.test.ts -t "releaseAll\|same id"` | red (releaseAll missing) | Kill the Electron renderer process (its name in Activity Monitor, not verified yet) mid-take, then record again: the new take must start clean. |
| Stop keeps encoding through the poster wait | `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.test.tsx -t "stops encoding"` | red | Record a clip, press Stop at once, compare `ffprobe` durations of the file and its video stream: the gap should not grow past the stop. |
| Metadata failure leaves an orphan `.mp4` | `npx vitest run src/main/recording/recording-writer.test.ts -t "metadata failure"` | red (EISDIR) | Not practical: needs a sidecar write failure. |
| Window closed during countdown keeps the take pending | `npx vitest run src/main/recording/recording-hub.test.ts -t "window closed during a countdown"` | passes (`forceReset` already worked) | **The bug was the wiring in `index.ts`**, not covered by a unit test. Start a recording, close the window with the red button during 3-2-1, then open the tray: "Record" must be enabled again. On `main` it stays disabled. |
| Crash during countdown leaves the app hidden | `npx vitest run src/main/recording/recording-hub.test.ts -t "forced reset that reveals"` | red | Start a countdown on a region, kill the renderer process during 3-2-1: the app must come back to the window. |

Full run on this branch: `npx vitest run` → 2617 passed, 1 failed. The failure moves between runs inside `capture-overlay.test.tsx` (timing under load, unrelated); that file passes alone (115/115). `bun run check-types`: no errors. `verify:local` (the pre-push hook): passes; lint shows the same 17 warnings as `main`.

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:282`** — the cancel-in-the-gap check runs after `recordingCreate` resolves. Decide whether throwing there (caught by the existing `catch` → `discardStart`) is the right exit, or whether the abort should be explicit.
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-writer.ts:208-236`** — after the move, a metadata failure takes the `.mp4` back to staging (`takeBack`) and keeps the session `stranded`, so the save dialog can salvage it. Check that `takeBack` never deletes the only copy: it only calls `vault.remove` once the move back succeeded.
3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-writer.ts:273`** — `releaseAll` keeps the partial `.part` on disk (only the handle is released). This is a retention choice: `abort()` deletes, `releaseAll()` does not. Decide if crashed takes should stay on disk.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/index.ts:272` vs `:371`** — `closed` calls `forceReset()` without reveal (the user closed the window, do not reopen it); `render-process-gone` calls it with `revealAbandoned: true`. This is the policy decision for finding 2 and 9.
5. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:399-404`** — `stop()` pauses both sources before the poster-frame race. Confirm that nothing after the stop request should reach the file, and that pausing the audio source does not cut a real tail.

**Safe to skim:** the test files (they restate the behaviour above), and `recorder-store.ts:260` (the id format change, one line).

## Checks

- `npx vitest run` (apps/kaipu-record) — 2617 passed, 1 failed (flaky `capture-overlay`, passes alone)
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json` and `-p tsconfig.web.json` — no errors
- `bun run verify:local` (pre-push) — passed
- `oxlint src` — 0 errors, 17 warnings (same as `main`)

## Manual verification

- [ ] Close the main window with the red button during the 3-2-1 countdown: the tray "Record" is enabled again right after.
- [ ] Kill the renderer process during a recording, then record again: the second take starts clean, and no `kaipu-rec-*.mp4.part` from the dead take is reused.
- [ ] Kill the renderer process during a countdown on a region: the app window comes back.
- [ ] Press Stop about 0.5 s after the start: the saved video's stream duration is not longer than the `durationSeconds` shown in the library by more than the frame's own duration.
